name: Teach Your Child to Read in 100 Easy Lessons (Engelmann, Haddox & Bruner)

principles: Scripted, step-by-step lessons that remove teacher guesswork — every word the parent says is written out
Modified orthography (Distar alphabet) to make English phonetically regular for beginning readers before transitioning to standard print
Sounds taught before letter names — decoding is the central skill, not letter identification
Continuous blending (say the word slowly without pausing between sounds, then say it fast) rather than choppy segmenting
Built-in error correction procedures for every task type — the program anticipates exactly how a child might fail and scripts the fix

knowledgeBankGaps.title: Direct Instruction (DISTAR) — Engelmann Method
knowledgeBankGaps.summary: Highly structured, scripted teaching method where every word the teacher says is prescribed. Based on the principle that if a child fails, the communication was unclear, not the child. Uses carefully sequenced examples, built-in error correction, and modified orthography (joined letters, macrons) to teach reading through systematic phonics. Adapted from SRA's Distar Fast Cycle Reading Program for home use.

knowledgeBankGaps.title: 100 Easy Lessons Format — Scripted Daily Reading
knowledgeBankGaps.summary: Each lesson is a single 20-minute session with 5-10 numbered tasks: sounds introduction, say-it-fast (oral blending), say-the-sounds (segmenting), word reading (arrow-and-ball notation), rhyming, story reading with comprehension questions, picture comprehension, and sounds writing (letter formation). Parent reads red text verbatim; child responses are indicated. Correction procedures boxed inline.

mappings.curriculumTopic: Individual letter sounds (m, s, a, e, t, etc.) taught one at a time in isolation
th, sh, wh, ch taught as single sounds
Sliding finger along arrow, saying sounds without pausing, then saying the word fast
Parent says compound word in parts, child blends: motor...boat → motorboat
mappings.note: Oral-only precursor to written blending — same Homa topic but earlier scaffold

mappings.curriculumTopic: Words like mat, sat, am, eat, rat read with arrow notation
Modified orthography: macrons for long vowels (ā, ē, ī, ō), joined letters for digraphs
ou/ow sounds (loud, owww)
ar, er/or sounds (car, brother)
Change onset, keep rime: m→at, r→at (Lessons 3+)
Word families used in rhyming tasks (at, am, eat families)
Say-the-sounds tasks: child segments am → aaa-mmm
said, have, old, give — irregularly spelled words introduced after lesson ~40
Arrow reading: slow sounding then fast reading, progressing to reading 'the fast way'
Second reading + comprehension questions (who, what, why, prediction)
Look at the picture, answer questions about what you see + predict
What do you think will happen? questions after story reading
Sounds writing: trace model letter then write 3-5 independently
Capital letters introduced later in the program
Picture comprehension questions link story to child's life (Did you ever go fishing?)
Understanding that letters represent sounds, left-to-right tracking via arrow notation, transition from Distar orthography to standard print
Say-it-fast compound word tasks (motor+boat, ice+cream) in early oral blending
Parent reads story sentences aloud during first reading, asks comprehension questions during second reading
Terms: sounds, words, sentences, rhyming, sounding out, reading the fast way
Lesson 77+: transition from sounds to letter names. Child learns full alphabet names and identifies letters whose names don't match their sounds (c, g, h, w, x, y, q).

Lesson 77+: long vowel rule taught explicitly — 'These words have an e on the end. The e doesn't make a sound. But you can tell how to say the rest of the word by saying the letter names.'  side, take, smile, bite, lake, five, nine, fine, late.
Words with -ing, -ed, -er, -est endings appear throughout lessons 62-100 (hunting, stopping, getting, shopping, sitting, sleeping, talked, started, lived).
Contractions appear in later stories: 'I'm', 'can't', 'don't', 'I'll', 'couldn't'

layer3_structure.weeklyTemplate: One lesson per day, 5 days/week. Each lesson contains 5-10 task types in fixed order: sounds introduction → say-it-fast (oral blending) → say-the-sounds (segmenting) → word reading (arrow notation) → rhyming → sounds review → story reading → second reading with comprehension → picture comprehension → sounds writing. Not all tasks appear in every lesson.
layer3_structure.reviewRhythm: No formal assessment. Mastery is continuous: correction procedures repeat the step until the child responds correctly. If a child struggles with a lesson, repeat it the next day. Built-in review via cycling previously learned sounds/words in every new lesson.
layer3_structure.notes: 100 lessons at 5/week = 20 weeks. Program designed to be completed within about two-thirds of a school year. The Engelmann approach is that if you follow the script precisely, the child will read at the end. Lessons 1-16 focus on oral skills and sound introduction. Lessons 17+ add stories. Lessons ~60-100 transition from modified to standard orthography. By lesson 100, child reads simple stories with standard English.

activityTypes.description: Parent points to a large letter with arrow, models the sound, child repeats. Modified orthography (macrons for long vowels, joined letters for digraphs). One new sound per lesson.

suggestedRecipe.name: distar-sound-card
suggestedRecipe.description: Large single letter or digraph in Distar orthography with arrow underneath (ball at start, arrow pointing right). Macron or joining marks where needed. Blank space below for child to trace. Black on white, very clean, minimal page.

activityTypes.description: Oral-only activity: parent says compound word or multi-syllable word in parts, child blends orally. No printed page needed — pure verbal exercise.

suggestedRecipe.name: oral-blending-prompt-card
suggestedRecipe.description: Parent prompt card with word pairs printed in large text, split by a divider line. e.g. 'motor | boat → motorboat'. Not for the child to see — parent reference only. Could be flash-card format.

activityTypes.description: Words printed large with dots under each sound and an arrow running left-to-right. Child touches first ball, sounds out slowly along arrow, then reads fast. The core DISTAR reading exercise.

suggestedRecipe.name: distar-word-reading
suggestedRecipe.description: Page with 6-10 words in large bold font, each with a horizontal arrow underneath and dots (balls) at each sound position. Child traces finger along arrow while blending. Uses Distar-style orthography marks (macrons, joined letters, small/large distinction). Clean black-and-white layout, one column.

activityTypes.description: Short decodable stories (5-15 sentences) using only sounds the child has learned, printed in large Distar orthography that transitions toward standard print. Comprehension questions follow.

suggestedRecipe.name: decodable-story-page
suggestedRecipe.description: Story text in large font with underlined and arrow-tracked sentences for the child to read. Initially uses Distar orthography (joined letters, macrons) that fades toward standard print in later lessons. Comprehension questions in a sidebar or below the story. Illustration area at bottom or side.

activityTypes.description: Black-and-white illustration related to the story. Parent asks open-ended questions about the picture to build inference and prediction skills.
activityTypes.note: Existing coloring-page recipe can serve as the illustration, with comprehension prompts added

activityTypes.description: Trace a model letter, then write it 3-5 times independently on a line. Two letters per lesson (one per line). Error feedback from parent.
Parent points to sounds, child changes onset to generate rhymes (m-at → mat, r-at → rat, s-at → sat). Printed letter-arrow format.

suggestedRecipe.name: onset-rime-drill
suggestedRecipe.description: Page with a rime (e.g. 'at') in large text with arrow. Onset letters listed to the left. Child combines onset + rime and reads the word. Arrows and dots for tracking. 6-8 word families per page.

activityTypes.description: Page of individual sounds (6-10) each with an arrow. Child says each sound. Mixes new and previously learned sounds for review.

suggestedRecipe.name: sound-review-grid
suggestedRecipe.description: Grid of individual letters/digraphs, each with a small arrow underneath. 2-3 columns, 3-5 rows. Child says the sound for each. Mix of recently introduced and review sounds. Clean, high-contrast black-and-white.

activityTypes.description: End-of-program graded book list (20 titles from Eric Carle to Magic Tree House). Each book lists vocabulary words to pre-teach. Parent reads book aloud first, then teaches words, then child reads independently.

suggestedRecipe.name: recommended-reading-card
suggestedRecipe.description: Card per book: cover thumbnail, title/author, grade level indicator, vocabulary words to teach, reading steps. Printable set for the reading shelf.

notes: This is a heavyweight curriculum ingestion. 'Teach Your Child to Read in 100 Easy Lessons' is one of the most popular homeschool phonics programs ever published — over 500K copies sold. Its DISTAR method is research-backed (Project Follow Through) and uniquely structured among phonics programs. The key differentiator is the scripted, sequential, mastery-based approach with modified orthography. Every single topic in the curriculum maps to existing Homa taxonomy — the gap is entirely in activity formats/recipes (the arrow-and-ball notation, the decodable story format) and methodology knowledge, not in subject matter coverage. The 120-page PDF is a scan (all images, no extractable text). The program targets ages 4-5 (bright 3s through struggling older readers). 22 taxonomy topics mapped with 100% coverage. Part 2 PDF (lessons 62-100) dropped separately by Aless on 2026-07-19 10:44 EDT, ingested to verify later-program features.
